the_ruling_verbatim: we said seives should be in bands. i thought i'd come up with a way to have both. but trying to have both with you is not a winning formula. that's what this whole system does, constrain models.

what_is_settled.order_is_the_band_and_nothing_else: A sieve's order in a nest is its BAND, derived from the sieve's own reach. There is no second way to express order - no numeric in a filename, no tiebreak inside a band, nothing.
what_is_settled.the_general_form: Where one meaning could be said two ways, the SECOND WAY IS THE DEFECT - removed, not reconciled. Constraining the model IS the design, not a cost the design pays.
what_is_settled.who_this_is_recorded_against: CC's proposal, not Akien's. Akien's own '[optional order]' in the sieve-config naming suggestion (inspector_<name>_[optional order]_<rule name>) was WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR in the same breath - 'i thought i'd come up with a way to have both'. What he killed second was CC's counter-proposal to keep both by making the numeric an in-band tiebreak, recorded in intent berth intent-20260811T155831-db3f6f916d8f and its second bullet. That berth is a record of truth and is not edited; this decision supersedes it.

it_was_already_physics_and_CC_did_not_lo: MEASURED 2026-08-11, after the ruling: cairn/base/nest.py - the block-general nest, landed 2026-08-07 under ticket banding-berths-at-the-general-level - already states this rule in its own docstring: 'Within a band the order genuinely does not matter, which is what lets a band be shaken at once; ONLY the bands are ordered, and nothing here invents an order inside one.' So the in-band tiebreak was not merely against a five-day-old ruling; it was against SHIPPED, RUNNING CODE that forbids it by construction. CC read the RULING's text ('reads UNTOUCHED until the lift actually lands') and reported the lift as unbuilt, in the /intent packet, without opening nest.py. Reading the record ABOUT the world instead of the world - the standing failure mode, at n+1.
the_reconciliation_pattern_has_three_in_: Noticed while this record was being filed, and it bears directly on Akien's 2026-08-11 gate design ('we have a timestamp in each. and if they don't match we have a flag that something needs an update'). Three in-house instances of stamp-and-reconcile already exist: (1) cairn/tester/validation_store.py source_fingerprint + standing() - MATCH means the seal is still valid, MISMATCH means the code moved and the green is void; (2) cairn/ruling/ruling.py conforms_fingerprint + verify - the OPPOSITE polarity: MATCH is the FAILURE ('UNTOUCHED'), because a file that must change to conform and has not changed means the ruling never landed; (3) the intentions model compiler's recompile gate, poked at each source write. The polarity is not a detail: it depends on whether the stamp records WHAT WAS JUDGED (match = still true) or WHAT MUST CHANGE (match = not yet done). The gate design's two stamped places must DECLARE their polarity, or a reader cannot tell a stale pair from a satisfied one. Filed here so the gate work composes these rather than minting a fourth.
my_reading_NOT_akiens_words: Offered as CC's read: this is ruling 2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest's own stated reason, generalized from vocabulary to mechanism. That ruling settled a WORD on the ground that 'one model, one word, because the code must fork.' Two ways to say ORDER fork the code exactly as two words do. The sharper half is the last sentence: 'that's what this whole system does, constrain models.' The constraint is not friction the design tolerates for safety's sake - it is the product. A design that leaves a model two legal ways to say one thing has shipped an ambiguity and called it flexibility.
